_comment: Seed snapshot for status.html. In production a periodic polling agent
overwrites this file next to the published page from the deployment's
/health/ready and /metrics endpoints (cadence in
docs/operations/incident-response.md, private repository). The committed copy declares no
state on purpose: the page used to hardcode five green 'Operational'
badges and a clean incident history while telling visitors they
reflected a published snapshot that did not exist.
published_at  RFC 3339. Until it is set, the page shows 'No snapshot
published' and renders none of the sections below.
components    {key: state}. Keys must match the data-component
attributes in status.html: api, dashboard,
document-storage, background-workers, sso.
state is one of: operational, degraded, outage.
A key that is absent or unrecognised stays 'No data'.
incidents     [{title, status, started_at, resolved_at, impact,
summary}]. An empty array renders 'No incidents
reported'; omitting the key leaves the no-snapshot
wording, because 'we published nothing' and 'we looked
and found none' are different claims.
maintenance   [{title, scheduled_for, expected_impact}]. Same
empty-vs-absent distinction.
All values render as text, never as markup.
